scope: WP17 checkout-local service-aware uninstall for an existing supervised profile on Linux systemd --user
Manifest-v3 source attestation, exact target-profile archive binding, clean Web replacement, service acceptance, crash recovery and cleanup residue retry
Preservation rather than revocation of durable state outside the archived target profile

supportedBoundary.source: checkout-local or sibling lifecycle helper only
supportedBoundary.sourceProfile: an installer-managed supervised target profile whose installed cohort exposes the required read-only operator and lifecycle-attestation seams
supportedBoundary.targetProfileLocalSemantics: Uninstall deactivates and archives the named managed profile locally, then installs an exact clean Web profile under the same profile name. It is not a whole-DSH_HOME erase, identity revocation, credential revocation, external-state retirement or guarantee that another profile sharing retained state cannot interpret it later.
supportedBoundary.archiveScope: the complete named profile directory tree as copied from the stopped source and bound by profile/tree digests
supportedBoundary.replacementScope: an installer-clean Web profile at the same target-profile path
supportedBoundary.operatorResponsibility: The operator must stop every external or manually started process using DSH_HOME. The installer controls only systemd units whose ownership it can prove.
supportedBoundary.nonLinux: unsupported and fail closed before lifecycle mutation
supportedBoundary.noService: unsupported and fail closed before lifecycle mutation

releaseBoundary.behavior: The released remote bootstrap still carries zero sentinel lifecycle-helper hashes, so remote supervised uninstall fails closed before downloading or executing lifecycle helpers. This record proves only checkout-local behavior.

implementation: The public local lifecycle path admits supervised uninstall only for Linux systemd --user service management; non-Linux and --no-service combinations are rejected before lifecycle mutation, and uninstall performs no npm registry or pnpm-store work.

The source cohort is capability-probed before registry, Store, systemd or transaction mutation. After installer-owned units are stopped, a read-only supervised operator attests Delivery owner bindings, Recovery state and Automations state without opening a migrating Store.

The stopped source target-profile tree digest and compact operator proofs are manifest-bound before the home copy. The copied target profile must retain the exact tree digest before it can be moved into uninstalled-profiles/<profile>-<timestamp>-<transaction-id>.

The archive proof covers the complete target-profile directory tree. The compact operator proof is deliberately narrower: it binds only the protocol-defined Delivery, Recovery, Automations, owner and unmanaged-Automation projections. That negative proof is not evidence that every byte, private state path or effect anywhere in DSH_HOME was enumerated or retired.

The staged target is replaced with an installer-clean Web profile and activated offline. Supervised uninstall does not run the upgrade preview/active plan and does not require Lark or supervised active attestation after those capabilities have been removed.

Originally active installer-managed units must return with fresh InvocationIDs, exact accepted process/restart records and a stability window; originally inactive units remain inactive. Same-home dynamic units that are not in the accepted set remain persistently masked, disabled and inactive.

A crash before the swap boundary restores the original home and active set. A post-swap failure contains services and preserves current home, original home and manifest evidence rather than automatically rolling back possibly migrated state.

Recovery validates the operation/protocol/phase union, archive identity and digest, clean target digest, exact serviceAcceptance coverage, systemd ownership inventory and transaction bindings before external mutation. A retry after post-swap failure does not rerun archive creation or the source operator.

Cleanup recovery handles stale service acceptance by re-establishing bound masks and barriers, stopping the exact inventory, obtaining fresh InvocationID/journal/stability acceptance, durably replacing the acceptance proof and resuming the existing cleanup without repeating package, archive or supervised-operator work.

Crash recovery explicitly covers cleanup prepared, deleting and metadata-only phases, masked inactive and active residues, and both mask-path versus daemon-reload cache-skew directions. Raw systemd identity, numeric fields and stable state tuples fail closed before mutation.

Committed cleanup first tombstones and recursively deletes the original-home backup through descriptor-anchored traversal, then removes transaction residue. A metadata-only cleanup phase means only that the backup is already absent and transaction metadata remains to be removed; it is not proof that retained credentials, owner bindings, Session, Goal, databases, linger settings, unit files or external state were cleared.

securityAndTrustBoundaries.sameUidPathReplacement: Manifest loading opens and validates the transaction root through a directory fd, but closes that fd after the read; parts of recovery later resolve the transaction pathname again. Critical rename and cleanup paths have additional identity guards. Malicious same-UID pathname replacement and root are explicitly outside the claimed threat model.
securityAndTrustBoundaries.guardianFinalizeKillGap: The guardian completion token is sent after durable service acceptance, before mask/enablement finalization and transaction commit finish. A forced-kill regression now covers the resulting active-plus-bound-masked residue and proves a later retry performs fresh reacceptance and converges without repeating package, archive or supervised-operator work.
securityAndTrustBoundaries.negativeProofGranularity: The supervised source proof is a schema-defined projection and must not be described as a proof of absence across the whole home. The archived profile tree digest is broader but still target-profile-local.
securityAndTrustBoundaries.metadataCleanupGranularity: A cleanup-started metadata-only state records that original-home is already absent and only transaction metadata remains. Removing that residue does not revoke or delete durable state intentionally retained outside the archived target profile.

engineeringValidation.acceptanceRule: The frozen tree passed workspace validation, zero-warning lint, typechecking, root and recursive package tests, final build, and dry-run packing for every plugin and shared package.

independentReview.interpretation: The final frozen release review found no BLOCK or HIGH defect in the documented checkout-local threat model. Same-UID malicious pathname replacement, whole-home negative proof, external-state retirement and real-environment validation remain explicit claim boundaries rather than silently accepted properties.

supported: The checkout contains a bounded Linux systemd --user supervised-uninstall path with strict dispatch, source attestation, target-profile archive binding, clean Web replacement, service acceptance and recovery contracts.
The frozen full installer suite passed 276 tests with one release-sentinel conditional skip and has a retained log whose SHA-256 is recorded.
The frozen repository root check passed workspace validation, zero-warning lint, typechecking, root and recursive tests, final build and 33 dry-run packs.
The target-profile archive and exact clean replacement are distinct from intentionally retained durable and external state.
Remote supervised uninstall remains fail closed under the current zero-sentinel release.

limitations: No complete real supervised DSH_HOME uninstall transaction was executed in this batch.
No real systemd --user stop, mask, home swap, fresh InvocationID, journal readiness, stability or crash-recovery sequence was observed for this batch.
No real Lark WebSocket, cloud credential, cloud application or production message flow was exercised.
The three live-WAL databases were not exercised through a real cross-inode lifecycle copy and uninstall archive.
Non-Linux, --no-service and external-supervisor supervised uninstall remain unsupported.
The current release uses zero sentinel lifecycle-helper hashes, so remote supervised uninstall remains unpublished and fail closed.
The implementation does not claim protection against malicious same-UID processes or root.
The tested guardian-finalization crash windows do not prove every possible kernel, systemd or host failure interleaving.
The operator negative proof is not a whole-home proof, and metadata-only cleanup is not external-state retirement.
WP17 remains implementing and the complete 18-work-package objective remains incomplete.
